title: 28-Layer Stack with Differential Evolution and Latin Hypercube Initialization
scientific_hypothesis: Global optimization with differential evolution and Latin Hypercube sampling will escape local optima that trapped the gradient-based optimizer in prior iterations, achieving higher target scores by exploring multi-modal interference landscapes more thoroughly.
design_principle: Replace gradient-based local search with population-based global search. Initialize thickness population using Latin Hypercube distribution spanning ±20% of iteration_07's observed thickness range (45-201 nm for HfO2, 45-73 nm for SiO2). Maintain alternating HfO2/SiO2 sequence on fused silica substrate.
proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers)
design_variables: 28 layer thicknesses (14 HfO2 + 14 SiO2), each independently optimizable within expanded bounds
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Maintain robustness score > 0.35 under ±15% thickness perturbation
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds expanded to 40-240 nm for HfO2, 35-90 nm for SiO2 based on iteration_07 observations
Outermost layer should be SiO2 for environmental durability per evidence
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflectance bands
Global optimization explores configuration space more thoroughly than gradient descent for multi-modal problems
expected_advantages: Escapes local optima that limited prior gradient-based runs
Latin Hypercube ensures uniform coverage of thickness parameter space
Higher probability of finding globally optimal interference conditions
known_risks: Differential evolution requires more function evaluations, may need larger search budget
May converge slower in early generations before exploiting promising regions
execution_request_english: Optimize a 28-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2(1)|SiO2(2)|HfO2(3)|SiO2(4)|...|HfO2(27)|SiO2(28). Initialize 28 thickness variables using Latin Hypercube sampling with bounds: HfO2 layers 40-240 nm, SiO2 layers 35-90 nm. Use differential evolution optimizer with population size 50, mutation rate 0.8, crossover rate 0.9, maximum 500 generations. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Objective: maximize weighted sum of (mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band) and (mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band) with equal weights. Apply ±15% relative uniform thickness tolerance for robustness scoring. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for top 5 candidates. Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
revision_reason: Switched from gradient_thickness to differential_evolution optimizer per feedback directive. Expanded thickness bounds to ±20% of iteration_07 observed range (was 50-300 nm uniform, now 40-240 nm for HfO2, 35-90 nm for SiO2). Added Latin Hypercube initialization for better parameter space coverage.
